stem: A client has a normal BMI but an elevated waist circumference. Why is the waist measurement still clinically useful in preventive risk assessment?

options.A: Waist circumference adds little useful adiposity information once BMI falls within the normal range for an adult.
options.B: A normal BMI removes the need to consider abdominal adiposity when assessing excess-adiposity-related cardiometabolic risk.
options.C: A larger waist circumference generally reflects greater lean muscle mass and therefore indicates lower cardiometabolic risk.
options.D: Waist circumference complements BMI by assessing abdominal adiposity and helps characterize cardiometabolic risk related to excess adiposity.

rationale: The 2026 AHA/ACC/ADA/ASN CKM guideline recommends assessing overweight/obesity and abdominal adiposity with both BMI and waist circumference to characterize risk related to excess adiposity. Therefore waist circumference provides complementary information even when BMI alone is not elevated. D is correct. A and B incorrectly treat BMI as sufficient by itself, and C reverses the clinical meaning of increased abdominal adiposity.
educational_objective: Explain why waist circumference complements BMI when assessing abdominal adiposity and excess-adiposity-related cardiometabolic risk.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology / American Diabetes Association / American Society of Nephrology
source_document_title: 2026 AHA/ACC/ADA/ASN Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome — Top Things to Know
source_version_date: Updated June 9, 2026; live official AHA page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Top Things to Know, item 6 — Assess and Treat Overweight and Obesity: assess overweight/obesity and abdominal adiposity with both BMI and waist circumference to characterize risk related to excess adiposity.
source_claim_supported: Current CKM guidance recommends both BMI and waist circumference because waist measurement adds information about abdominal adiposity and excess-adiposity-related risk.
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — prevention and early detection of health problems and assessment of risk factors.
correction_summary: Balanced option lengths and preserved the 2026 guideline recommendation to use waist circumference together with BMI for excess-adiposity risk characterization.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — the June 2026 AHA/ACC/ADA/ASN guideline explicitly recommends both BMI and waist circumference; D uniquely reflects that recommendation.
